-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem nat_prime_iff_no_proper_divisors (n : Nat) :
    Nat.Prime n ↔
      n > 1 ∧ ∀ d : Nat, 1 < d ∧ d < n → n % d ≠ 0 := by
  rw [Nat.prime_def_lt]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hn, hdiv⟩
    constructor
    · omega
    · intro d hd hmod
      have hdvd : d ∣ n :=
        (Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero).2 hmod
      have hd_eq_one : d = 1 :=
        hdiv d hd.2 hdvd
      omega
  · rintro ⟨hn, hproper⟩
    constructor
    · omega
    · intro d hdlt hdvd
      by_contra hdne
      have hnpos : 0 < n := by
        omega
      have hdpos : 0 < d :=
        Nat.pos_of_dvd_of_pos hdvd hnpos
      have hdgt : 1 < d := by
        omega
      exact (hproper d ⟨hdgt, hdlt⟩)
        ((Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero).1 hdvd)
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem check_prime_postcond_satisfied (n : Nat) (h_precond : check_prime_precond n) :
    check_prime_postcond n (check_prime n h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  change
    decide (Nat.Prime n) = true ↔
      (n > 1 ∧ ∀ d : Nat, 1 < d ∧ d < n → n % d ≠ 0)
  rw [decide_eq_true_eq]
  exact nat_prime_iff_no_proper_divisors n
  -- !benchmark @end proof

Your task is to implement the "Optimized Trial Division" primality test algorithm and verify its functional correctness in Lean. Given a non-negative integer n, determine whether n is prime by dividing it by integers from 2 up to sqrt(n). Postconditions: Returns true iff n > 1 and has no divisors between 2 and n-1. This requires stating and proving the number-theoretic lemma: if n is composite, it has a factor less than or equal to its square root.
